# Coverage & taxonomy

This document is the map of **what RedBlueSkills covers, what it will cover, and the
exact fields every skill is labeled with**. It has two halves:

1. **The taxonomy** — every dimension a skill is classified on (surface, team,
   kill-chain stage, technique refs, risk, maturity) and the controlled vocabulary
   for each. This is the schema the validator (`tools/validate.py`) enforces; the
   authoritative definition lives in [`SKILL-SPEC.md`](SKILL-SPEC.md).
2. **The coverage map** — which cells of *(surface × kill-chain stage)* are filled
   today, which are planned, and the per-surface source frameworks we map to. The
   website renders this same data as a radial map (colored where covered, dark where
   planned) plus a coverage matrix.

---

## 1. The fields every skill is classified on

Each `SKILL.md` opens with YAML frontmatter. These are the classification fields and
the values they may take. (Operational body sections — Overview, Procedure,
Validation, etc. — are specified in [`SKILL-SPEC.md`](SKILL-SPEC.md).)

### `app_type` — the target surface

The kind of system the skill targets. One directory per surface under `skills/`.

| Value | Status | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| `web-app` | **shipping** (reference implementation) | OWASP Top 10 (web) |
| `api` | **shipping** | OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023) |
| `cloud-native` | **shipping** (opened) | Cloud/container attack surface; MITRE ATT&CK Cloud & Containers |
| `ci-cd` | **shipping** (opened) | OWASP Top 10 CI/CD Security Risks |
| `mobile` | **shipping** (opened) | OWASP MASVS / Mobile Top 10 |
| `network` | **shipping** (opened) | Network services & lateral movement; MITRE ATT&CK + NIST SP 800-53 / CSF + CIS Controls v8 |
| `llm-ai` | **shipping** (opened) | LLM/GenAI applications & agents; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Apps 2025 + MITRE ATLAS |

### `team` — offense, defense, or joint

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `red` | Offensive — finds and proves a weakness. `authorization: required`. |
| `blue` | Defensive — hardens or detects. `authorization: not-required` (passive). |
| `purple` | Joint / detection-engineering spanning both. May use any stage. |

Every red skill is **paired** with a blue skill (and vice versa) via `pairs_with`,
and the pairing is **bidirectional** — the validator fails the build otherwise. That
pairing is the core discipline of this library: no offense without the matching
defense.

### `killchain.stage` — where in the kill chain

Offensive stages (Unified Kill Chain, condensed) and defensive stages (NIST-aligned)
share one namespace so red and blue sort side by side.

| Offense (`red`) | Defense (`blue`) |
|---|---|
| `recon` | `harden` |
| `initial-access` | `detect` |
| `execution` | `respond` |
| `persistence` | `recover` |
| `privilege-escalation` | `hunt` |
| `defense-evasion` | |
| `credential-access` | |
| `lateral-movement` | |
| `collection` | |
| `exfiltration` | |
| `impact` | |

### `techniques` — external framework references

At least one reference id total. These make each skill traceable to the standard
taxonomies and drive the technique-coverage roll-up in the orchestrator.

| Key | Vocabulary | Who uses it |
|---|---|---|
| `attack` | MITRE ATT&CK technique / sub-technique ids (`T1190`, `T1552.005`) | required — all skills |
| `capec` | CAPEC attack-pattern ids (`CAPEC-66`) | optional |
| `cwe` | CWE weakness ids (`CWE-89`) | optional |
| `owasp` | OWASP Top 10 ids (`A03:2021`) | optional |
| `d3fend` | MITRE D3FEND defensive-technique ids (`D3-UBA`) | blue skills **should** list these |

### `risk` — blast radius of *running* the skill

| Field | Vocabulary |
|---|---|
| `level` | `info` \| `low` \| `medium` \| `high` \| `critical` |
| `reversible` | does running it leave lasting change on the target? |
| `data_touch` | `none` \| `read` \| `read-write` |

### `maturity` — how proven the skill is

```
draft ──review──▶ reviewed ──validate──▶ validated ──(6mo / breaking change)──▶ stale
```

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `draft` | authored, not yet reviewed. Excluded from the default catalog. |
| `reviewed` | a maintainer has read it for correctness and safety. |
| `validated` | proven end-to-end against a named target; carries a `validation` block (`method`, `target`, `last_validated`, `validated_by`). Only `validated` skills are recommended for production. |
| `stale` | was validated, but drifted — CI flags this when `last_validated` is > ~6 months old. |

A `validated` skill names its lab in the `validation.target` field. Current targets
in use: `owasp-crapi`, `owasp-juice-shop`, `docker-colima`, `ec2-metadata-mock`,
`minio-s3`, `ci-local` (a dependency-free git+bash CI lab, `_lab/ci-local/`),
`llm-local` (a dependency-free stdlib-Python mock-LLM lab, `_lab/llm-local/`).

## 2. What each surface maps to

Every surface is anchored to an authoritative framework so coverage is measurable
rather than ad-hoc.

- **`web-app`** → **OWASP Top 10 (web).** The reference implementation: 10 red↔blue
  pairs across the core (injection, XSS, SSRF, XXE, IDOR/access control, broken
  auth, CSRF, path traversal, command injection, HTTP fingerprinting).
- **`api`** → **OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023), API1–API10.** BOLA, broken
  authentication, BOPLA/excessive-data-exposure, unrestricted resource consumption,
  BFLA, unrestricted access to sensitive business flows, SSRF, security
  misconfiguration, improper inventory management, unsafe consumption of APIs.
- **`cloud-native`** → **cloud & container attack surface.** IMDS credential theft,
  public object-storage exposure, privileged-container escape, cloud IAM persistence
  (T1098), and Kubernetes RBAC abuse — mapped across MITRE ATT&CK Cloud/Containers,
  MITRE D3FEND, NIST SP 800-53 / SP 800-190, the NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guide,
  and CIS Benchmarks.
- **`ci-cd`** → **OWASP Top 10 CI/CD Security Risks.** Poisoned pipeline execution,
  insufficient credential hygiene, dependency-chain abuse, artifact
  integrity/provenance, insecure system configuration (runner abuse).
- **`mobile`** → **OWASP MASVS / Mobile Top 10.** Insecure data storage (M9),
  hardcoded secrets (M1/M7), weak transport / missing cert-pinning (M5), insecure
  deep links (M4/M8), and mobile-to-backend API abuse (M3).
- **`network`** → **network services & lateral movement.** Service/port exposure
  (T1046), exposed-service exploitation (T1190/T1210), TLS/certificate weakness
  (SP 800-52r2), credential sniffing & layer-2 AiTM (T1040/T1557), and lateral
  movement (T1021/T1550) — mapped across MITRE ATT&CK, MITRE D3FEND, NIST SP 800-53
  Rev 5 / CSF 2.0, and CIS Controls v8.
- **`llm-ai`** → **OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025.** Prompt injection
  (LLM01), sensitive information disclosure (LLM02), excessive agency (LLM06),
  system prompt leakage (LLM07), and unbounded consumption (LLM10) — 5 red↔blue
  pairs mapped to MITRE ATLAS, MITRE ATT&CK, MITRE D3FEND, and NIST SP 800-53
  Rev 5, and validated end-to-end against the dependency-free `llm-local` mock-LLM
  lab (`_lab/llm-local/`).
